name: haxe-inactive-regions
description: Greys out Haxe code that is excluded by #if / #elseif / #else conditional compilation.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In untrusted workspaces the Haxe compiler is not run; defines are estimated from the hxml files instead.

haxeInactiveRegions.enabled.description: Grey out code excluded by conditional compilation.

haxeInactiveRegions.opacity.description: Opacity of inactive code (0 = invisible, 1 = normal).

haxeInactiveRegions.compilerArgs.markdownDescription: Haxe compiler arguments describing the build whose defines decide what is active, e.g. `["build.hxml"]` or `["build.hxml", "-D", "foo"]`. When empty, vshaxe's active configuration is used (see `#haxeInactiveRegions.useVshaxeConfiguration#`), then the first entry of `#haxe.configurations#`, then `build.hxml`, then the first `.hxml` file in the workspace folder. If the arguments describe several builds (`--next`), the first one is used.

haxeInactiveRegions.useVshaxeConfigurati.markdownDescription: When the Haxe extension (vshaxe) is installed, use its active configuration (the one shown in its status bar, including Lime/OpenFL projects) unless `#haxeInactiveRegions.compilerArgs#` is set. Its defines include those of libraries and their dependencies, but not those added by initialization macros.

haxeInactiveRegions.defines.markdownDescription: Extra defines applied on top of the build's defines. Use `name`, `name=value`, or `!name` to undefine.

enumDescriptions: Ask the Haxe compiler for the exact defines (includes defines added by haxelibs); fall back to reading the hxml if that fails.
Never run the compiler; estimate defines from the hxml arguments (-D, -lib, target).
haxeInactiveRegions.definesSource.description: How to determine the active defines.

haxeInactiveRegions.haxePath.markdownDescription: Path to the Haxe executable. When empty, `#haxe.executable#` (vshaxe) is used, then a local lix shim, then `haxe` from the PATH.

haxeInactiveRegions.haxeVersion.markdownDescription: Haxe version used for `haxe_ver`, `haxe4` etc. when defines are estimated from hxml. When empty, `haxe --version` is used.
